messages:
maria: FYI ran a couple nsys + perfetto traces on the KV-cache regression from yesterday. attaching a quick timeline screenshot in the thread :point_down:

aj: saw the screenshot. main weirdness was a ~350ms hot block that we thought was prefetch, but kernel chooser shows it as matmul_eltwise.

sudhir: interesting — could be misgrouped ranges. did you include per-request NVTX ranges?

maria: No, I only had generic spans: `runtime:serve` and `kv:batch`. I think that made the long matmul appear as part of the request boundary.

olivia: that matches what we saw in the perf run on g5s — when batching causes cross-request aggregation the NVTX labels hide which kernels belong to which request.

ben: proposal: add per-request NVTX ranges at request enter/exit with a short stable id and a human label (e.g., `req=abcd123 handle:decode`). We can keep them low-overhead and truncated.

maria: agree. rough sketch: `nvtxRangePushA(req_label)` right before the scheduler picks kernels, pop after response enqueue. here's a snippet I tested: 

```cpp
// very small label, avoid heap allocs
char lbl[32];
snprintf(lbl, sizeof(lbl), "r:%x:%s", req_hash, stage_short);
nvtxRangePushA(lbl);
// ... do work ...
nvtxRangePop();
```

aj: two quick notes: 1) avoid embedding full prompts or user ids in labels (PII). 2) keep label length < 32 to avoid driver truncation.

perf-bot: sample-run 2111112230 complete — nsys profile saved to s3://redwood-perf/210111/nsys-r2111112230.qdrep

sudhir: we should also add a batch-level NVTX span when we coalesce requests so we can attribute kernels to batch vs request. Otherwise the KV prefetch kernel might look like request work when it's actually batch housekeeping.

olivia: +1. naming suggestion: `r:<hexid>`, `b:<batchid>`, `k:<short-kernel>` for small labels. e.g., `r:4f2a decode`, `b:9 prefetch`. keeps timeline compact.

ben: ops question: what's the worst-case overhead? did you measure extra 95th latency?

maria: quick microbench — adding push/pop per request added ~0.2ms median and ~0.6ms p99 in extreme small-request microbench. For our real workloads it's <0.1ms. still worth measuring in prod though.

aj: also add an opt-in sampling mode: only annotate 1 in N requests to avoid overload on high-QPS tenants. we can detect suspicious traces and then flip to full annotation for debugging.

maria: good idea. I can land a small PR: runtime NVTX helpers + config flag `nvtx_per_request_sampling_rate`. default 0 (off) for Dedicated, 1% for Hosted.

sudhir: also add a note for kernel-chooser: if `nvtx` request span exists prefer matching kernel attribution to ranges instead of coarse request span. helps when kernels run under different stream contexts.

olivia: for trace consumers (perfetto viewer): include a legend mapping short labels to full meanings in our trace README, and add a small script to synthesize a per-request timeline CSV.

ben: can you include a grep-friendly label pattern so our tracer tooling can extract req ids? e.g., `r:([0-9a-f]{4})`

maria: yes will follow that. final checklist for the PR: 
- add nvtx helper (C++/Rust shims)
- per-request push/pop
- batch push/pop around coalescer
- sampling flag + rate
- documentation and perf microbench numbers
- integration with kernel-chooser attribution rules

aj: lgtm. if you want I can review the attribution change after the NVTX helpers land.

maria: thanks — I'll draft the PR today and post the link here once CI passes.

perf-bot: queued perf regression job 2111112330 for nvtx-instrumentation branch

ben: nice. once we have a couple traces with per-request ranges we can re-run the problematic perfetto trace and see if that 350ms block splits into multiple requests or becomes an internal batch kernel.

maria: exactly the goal. will update with results. :rocket:
